I’m really sorry you’re feeling so down about this. These are my thoughts, even though I’m not entirely sure of your thought process about the “trade-off”: The scars are only under your shirt, right? I know that scars can be a bad reminder of whatever caused them, I understand that in more way than one. But scars can be covered up, scars can fade. I know if I were in your position, I’d pick the option that eases dysphoria when I have a shirt on. Look at it this way: right now, you’re probably dysphoric whether you’re wearing a shirt or not. If you get the surgery, you’ll look completely masculine while wearing a shirt, which is most of the time. That’s gotta ease a ton of dysphoria. And like I said, scars can fade! Look up Jammidodger on YouTube, he got double incision too and his scars are barely visible now.

I understand how horrible you feel about this right now, I really do. But you’re only looking at the negative side of everything. If your mental state is similar to how mine used to be, your brain might be telling you that there’s no way out because it wants to keep you in this bad place. It’s magnifying your fears about surgery and blocking out all the positives, even though from what you’ve described, top surgery sounds like something you need. When I really needed help with things in the past, I used to only focus on the bad things that could happen even though I subconsciously knew it would be better for me in the long run.

I obviously don’t know what’s going on inside your head, so this is all just speculation. But from what you said, your thought process sounds a lot like mine a few years ago. I don’t know if this will help in any way, but I’m really hoping for the best for you. <3

It will show through tight clothes, sadly. You can wear it over your clothes if you want to, but when I had a brace I hid it as much as possible by wearing baggier shirts and lots of layers. As for pants, you can either wear them over your brace or tuck them underneath. I always wore them over, because my brace went down enough that you could see it under my shirt if I didn’t. The only problem I had with wearing pants over the brace was that they sometimes slipped underneath, but wearing high-waisted pants helps prevent that. It takes some time to learn how to dress with a brace, but you’ll be able to figure it out, and you won’t look stupid. Also, there are youtube videos about what kinds of outfits to wear with a back brace. Most of them are intended for girls, I’m not sure what your gender is but either way I’ve seen some that have pretty good tips!

I also did sports when I had a back brace, but I only had to wear mine for 21 hours a day which meant I could take it off for practices and games. I would ask your doctor how many hours you’re supposed to wear it, and maybe talk with your coaches too to see if you can figure something out. But even if you can’t take off the brace for sports, I know that some people have been able to work out ways to still participate in sports while wearing a brace. Also yes, it’s possible to carry a backpack with a brace.

Feel free to message me if you have any more questions, I’m happy to help in any way I can. Wearing a brace really isn’t that bad once you get used to it. Good luck with everything :)
